course_note: French-language sections at uOttawa use parallel 17xx/27xx/37xx codes; the official catalogue confirms ADM 1701 Gestion et société, ADM 1705 Mathématiques pour la gestion, ADM 1740 Comptabilité financière, and ADM 1770 Applications des technologies de l'information en gestion (checked 2026-07-05). Remaining French pairings (ADM 1700 and the 27xx codes) follow the same convention but are still to_verify. Both codes in a pair map to the same skills. The official BTM program page confirms the BTM option includes the BCom compulsory core courses.

ADM 1300.name: Introduction to Business
ADM 1300.advice: An intro business course signals foundational knowledge, but it is weak evidence on its own — mention the team project or company analysis you did in it if it's relevant.

ADM 1301.name: Business and Society
ADM 1301.advice: Business & Society coursework can support research and stakeholder-awareness evidence if you name the analysis or case you produced.

ADM 1305.name: Mathematics for Management
ADM 1305.advice: Quantitative coursework only becomes evidence when you show it applied — an Excel model, a stats project, or an analysis with a conclusion.

ADM 1340.name: Financial Accounting
ADM 1340.advice: Financial Accounting coursework supports accounting fundamentals. To make it real evidence, name a concrete task: statements prepared, a case analyzed, or reconciliations done in the course or elsewhere.

ADM 1370.name: Applications of Information Technology for Business
ADM 1370.advice: ADM 1370 covers spreadsheets, databases, and business intelligence tools. A course code alone is weak evidence — add the actual deliverable (an Excel model, a database exercise, a BI dashboard) with the tool named.

ADM 2302.name: Business Analytics for Decision Making
ADM 2302.advice: ADM 2302 supports decision-modeling and analytics evidence. Turn it into a bullet: the business problem, the model or method (optimization, simulation, spreadsheet model), and the recommendation.

ADM 2303.name: Statistics for Management
ADM 2303.advice: Statistics coursework is weak evidence alone. If you analyzed a real dataset (in class or anywhere), state the dataset, method (regression, hypothesis testing), tool, and finding.

ADM 2304.name: Applications of Statistical Methods in Business
ADM 2304.advice: Applied statistics coursework becomes evidence when you show the applied part: the business dataset, the method, and what the analysis concluded.

ADM 2320.name: Marketing
ADM 2320.advice: The core Marketing course supports fundamentals only. A marketing plan project — with the target segment, channel choices, and any results or grades on the deliverable — is much stronger evidence.

ADM 2336.name: Organizational Behaviour
ADM 2336.advice: OB coursework supports people-management awareness. For HR roles, pair it with real coordination evidence: club recruitment, training coworkers, or running a team.

ADM 2337.name: Human Resource Management
ADM 2337.advice: HRM coursework signals HR interest; make it evidence by naming an HR case, policy analysis, or any real recruiting/onboarding you've done in clubs or jobs.

ADM 2341.name: Managerial Accounting
ADM 2341.advice: Managerial Accounting supports costing/budgeting fundamentals. Add the concrete task — a costing case, a budget built, a variance analysis — to move beyond course-only evidence.

ADM 2350.name: Financial Management
ADM 2350.advice: Financial Management coursework supports finance fundamentals. Name the model you built (valuation, capital budgeting, sensitivity analysis) and what decision it informed.

ADM 2372.name: Management Information Systems
ADM 2372.advice: ADM 2372 may support MIS knowledge, but a course name alone is not enough evidence for a business analyst role. If you completed a process analysis, systems project, or requirements document, add that project with tools, deliverables, and outcome.

ADM 2381.name: Business Communication Skills
ADM 2381.advice: Communication coursework is weak evidence by itself — a delivered presentation, report, or client-style deliverable with an audience is what counts.

ADM 3303.name: Hands-On Coding for Business
ADM 3303.advice: A coding-for-business course only counts once you show what you built — name the language, the business problem, and the working result.

ADM 3305.name: Business Simulation Analytics
ADM 3305.advice: Simulation analytics coursework becomes evidence when you describe the simulation, the decisions you modeled, and what the results showed.

ADM 3308.name: Business Data Mining
ADM 3308.advice: Data mining coursework is weak evidence alone — name the dataset, the technique, the tool, and the business finding to make it real.

ADM 3378.name: Emerging Topics in Management Information Systems
ADM 3378.advice: An emerging-MIS-topics course signals current tech-business awareness; cite the specific topic you researched or presented and the deliverable.

ADM 3379.name: Systems Analysis, Development, and Performance
ADM 3379.advice: Systems analysis coursework maps directly to business analyst work — add the system you analyzed, the requirements or process documents you produced, and any testing you did.

ADM 4103.name: Project Management
ADM 4103.advice: A project management course supports PM fundamentals; the evidence employers want is a real plan you built or a project you coordinated — scope, timeline, stakeholders, outcome.

ADM 4307.name: Business Forecasting Analytics
ADM 4307.advice: Forecasting coursework becomes evidence when you name what you forecasted, the method and tool, and how close or useful the forecast was.

ADM 4376.name: Cybersecurity Management
ADM 4376.advice: Cybersecurity management coursework is relevant to Ottawa's security sector — cite the risk assessment, policy analysis, or case you produced, not just the course.

ADM 4377.name: Digital Enterprise Systems and Strategies
ADM 4377.advice: Enterprise-systems coursework supports ERP/digital-transformation awareness; naming the system or case you worked on makes it credible.

ADM 4378.name: Business Communications Networks
ADM 4378.advice: Networks coursework signals technical literacy for business-technology roles; pair it with any hands-on lab, design, or analysis deliverable.

ADM 4379.name: Management and Implementation of Web Technologies in Organizations
ADM 4379.advice: Web-technologies coursework counts when you show the implementation or evaluation you did — the organization scenario, the technology, and the outcome.

facts: Telfer BCom co-op students complete 3-4 paid work terms (up to 16 months) alternating with study terms, starting after two years of study. (Verified against telfer.uottawa.ca/en/co-op/, 2026-07-05.)
Co-op is optional and admission is competitive, with a separate application in first year.
Co-op variants exist for BCom options including BTM, Finance, Accounting, and Management. Option-specific co-op pages: to_verify.
coop_context.advice: A co-op work term is direct, full-time student work experience — present it exactly like a job: employer, title, dates, and quantified bullets. If the posting is an internship, your co-op background is directly equivalent context; say 'co-op work term' explicitly.

AÉTSA.advice: AÉTSA work is student governance and operations evidence — name your portfolio, the budget or events you owned, who you coordinated with (school administration, sponsors, clubs), and the scale.

TCCT.advice: Your TCCT experience may support project coordination, stakeholder communication, event logistics, and business presentation skills. Make it stronger by adding the competition or event size, tools used, stakeholders coordinated, and a measurable outcome (placement, delegates sent, sponsorship raised).

BTA.advice: BTA involvement signals business-technology interest. It becomes real BTM/analytics evidence when you show organized tech or analytics events, workshop content, speaker or sponsor outreach, CRM/BI exposure, or attendance numbers.

TMA.advice: TMA involvement counts as marketing evidence only when the work is shown: campaign planning, social media content, event promotion, sponsorships, analytics, or audience growth with numbers.

TFS.advice: Finance club involvement becomes finance evidence when you show the technical work: stock pitches, modelling workshops you ran or completed, market research, Excel work, or competition results.

TAC.advice: Accounting club involvement supports CPA-pathway interest. Tax clinics, audit simulations, accounting cases, or events you ran (with attendance or volumes) turn it into real evidence.

HRA.advice: HR club involvement becomes HR evidence when you show recruitment drives, onboarding of members, event coordination, policy research, or HR case competitions.

UOCA.advice: Consulting club work counts when the analyst work is visible: case prep, client-style projects and presentations, research, stakeholder analysis, or firm workshops attended/organized.

Enactus.advice: Enactus projects are real project-execution evidence — state the project, beneficiaries or customers reached, revenue or funding involved, partners, and your specific role.

CASCO.advice: CASCO work (gala, fundraisers, sponsorship) is genuine event-operations and business-development evidence — include funds raised, attendance, sponsors secured, and team size.

BHS.advice: BHS involvement signals healthcare-business interest; panels organized, research produced, or partnerships built are what make it resume evidence.

TBJ.advice: TBJ work is writing and research evidence — cite published articles, interviews conducted, editing responsibility, or readership numbers.
TBJ.source_note: Confirmed via the AÉTSA Clubs at Telfer page (student-facing source), 2026-07-05.

TECDE.advice: Entrepreneurship club work counts when you show pitch competitions, customer discovery, market research, business model work, or sales outreach with numbers.

WMN.advice: WMN involvement supports leadership and community-building evidence — name events led, mentorship given or received, partnerships, and engagement numbers.

Telfer International.advice: Telfer International work supports cross-cultural communication — exchange-student support, international events, or multilingual communication are the evidence to surface.

ACE.advice: ACE project work counts as consulting/venture evidence when the project, client or venture, and outcome are named.

UOREC.full_name: University of Ottawa Real Estate Club (UOREC)
UOREC.advice: Real estate club involvement becomes finance evidence through property/market analyses, financial models, or industry events you organized.

TICC.advice: TICC participation is moderate evidence for case analysis and presentation. State the case topic, your recommendation, and any placement to strengthen it.

JDC.advice: JDC is a recognized inter-university competition — name your delegation category (academic case, sports, social), the case discipline, team role, and placement.

PALJ.advice: Place à la Jeunesse case work is bilingual case-competition evidence — state the case discipline, language, and result. It also demonstrates French business communication.

Happening Marketing.advice: Happening Marketing competition work is marketing case evidence — name the case, your analysis, and placement.

bilingual_context.advice: English/French bilingualism is a real asset in the Ottawa market (federal government, Crown corporations, and many NCR employers). If you are bilingual or in French Immersion, state it explicitly in your skills or summary — including your working level.
facts: The official BTM program page confirms a French Immersion stream is available with the BTM program (checked 2026-07-05).

evidence_strength_rules: Course code/name only = weak evidence at most.
Course + relevant project/task/tool mentioned = moderate evidence.
Course + concrete project + tool + deliverable/outcome = strong evidence.
Club membership only = weak evidence at most.
Club leadership title (VP, director, executive) = moderate evidence.
Club leadership + concrete tasks, metrics, stakeholders, tools, or outcomes = strong evidence.
Case competition participation = moderate evidence for problem solving, presentation, and teamwork; awards or organizing roles strengthen it.
Work terms, internships, jobs, and concrete projects always outweigh course-only evidence.
University context must never be used to rank students or compare schools.
